chapter: Lee and Lester Young band remembered
title: Billie Holiday in Los Angeles: Bumps, Jimmy Monroe and recording with her
summary: Billie fell for Bumps Myers and a man named Monroe rather than Lester; Rowles recalls her friendship with Lester and recording with her many times.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Lady Day fell for a guy out there. When she first came out there, she... Of course, she was alone. And everybody expected her to team up with Lester Young right away. That was taken for granted. But that didn't happen. And it was like Howdy-Doody time. It was real funny; it was such a surprise! And she went for the other tenor player, Bumps. And he started foolin' around with her, she went with him for a little while. Then she met a little guy, a little pimp, his name was Jimmy Monroe... I think that was his name.
Yes.
Is that the guy that owned the club up here?
Rowles - 45
That's his brother. Clark Monroe was the guy who had Monroe's at that time, and Jimmy was his brother.
Well, this guy was sort of a small fella...?
Yeah.
A very dapper, natty dresser.
Well, so was Clark. They called him the Black Clark Gable, because he was very handsome, and he had ...(?)...
Yeah. Well, Lady Day went for this guy.
That was his brother.
I think... That's once he started... I think.

Although some people say that was... She started going with Joe Guy, who was a trumpet player, and eventually they married. But nobody is sure about that. So she and Lester, did they see like old friends?

Oh yeah, they were buddies, right away. It was really great to watch. We used to have them come over to the house, you know, after work; they'd both come there, and she'd sing. She gave us... They had pictures outside, you know, with cardboard on the back. I used to rip them off and take them home. She'd sign them. I've still got them framed. But somebody stole my picture of Lester Young. I don't know why. It says... He started out, he says, 'Lester Young to Jimmy, my friend.' And somebody ripped it. And somebody ripped another picture. I had a picture
Rowles - 46

of Lady Day; it was the last record date she ever made out there, before she made Lady In Satin. It was with a small group, with Ben and Sweets. And there was a picture there; somebody snapped a picture of Lady Day, Red Mitchell and myself, right by the piano. I am in the middle; I'm at the piano. Red is here, she's here. And somebody stole it. It disappeared. It really breaks my heart.
Yeah, that's a shame.
But I have got a lot of pictures of Lady Day. I've got one picture here with her... Have you seen that picture of her with the tear in her eye?
No.
You know Paul Weinstein. He knows about it. It's quite a picture. She's listening to a playback. She was very sentimental.

I never had a fight with her once. I never had an argument with her. And I worked with her through the years... I don't know how many records I made with her. She'd ask for me all the time in preference to Oscar or anybody. "No," she says, "I want that little ofay, what's his name...Rowles." So I did all the recordings with her. I did an awful lot of them. But I never went on the road with her, and I'm glad I didn't, because that would have been...
